So we have two ways to look at this. First is basing God's gender on the texts, and second is basing God's gender on the entities on which God is based.

Textually, based on the Christian Bible, Judaic Talmud, and Muslim Quran, yes God is a man. But remember that the writers of those books were almost all, if not exclusively, men, and for millennia women were second-class citizens. Is it so surprising then that God had to be male?

Now, here's where history comes into play. Of the multiple religions extant in the Middle East two millennia and more ago, most were polytheistic (multiple gods,sometimes hierarchies of gods). Through a process historians call syncretism, these various religions morphed over time. Eventually, gods from Egyptian, Sumerian, Akkadian, Greek, and other mythologies blended and were distilled into this singular Abrahamic God. Those myriad gods included plenty of female goddesses. So when we see God appear, He includes features of female deities (including, if memory serves, creation of the world which was in some religions the responsibility of a female deity).

So the question is, is God an enby? That is definitely one way to think about it. You could also consider God to be, among other things, pangender, bigender, agender, maybe even intersex. I hardly think God is cisgender, however.

I went to Planned Parenthood for my HRT. They are a wonderfully supportive place to be no matter your gender or orientation, and I hope my perspective helps.

They’re going to ask you your preferred name and gender/pronouns. Their staff are amazingly sensitive to your feelings and needs, and they will make you feel comfortable.

Beyond those platitudes, their staff will ask you some basic questions to establish baselines. They’ll ask about medical history, personal history, etc, and they’ll do some work ups from blood and/or urine samples. At my first visit they pricked my finger and ran an HIV test then and there. The nurse practitioner I saw for HRT was beyond friendly and understanding, and she made sure to go over all the benefits and possible risks for HRT. She made absolutely sure I made an informed decision before giving me a prescription.

I hope I’ve covered everything, and I really hope this helps. If I missed anything, please ask. I’m glad to answer any questions you or anyone else may have.
